text:
Maya: Heads up — earlybird backfill queue spiked overnight, lots of late telemetry hitting recompute. console shows jobs queued but no per-tenant throttles in the UI.
Devin: saw that. current router is sending to dedicated pool A, which is saturated. we should consider routing to spare pool B as a temporary fallback.
Kevin: agree on fallback but we need quota guardrails. if we move requests to B we might violate reserved capacity for dedicated customers.
Anna: can we do a soft-throttle per-customer based on recent token spend? quick patch: cap reprocess qps per-tenant to 10 and queue the rest.
Leo: +1 for per-tenant soft-throttle. also we need clearer status in Console: percent complete + estimated remaining tokens. ops keeps DMing asking for ETA.
Maya: Console UX ask: add "recompute progress" panel and per-shard ETA. is that something product can toggle quickly?
Devin: product toggle = small backend flag + front-end panel. backend can emit metrics from the replay coordinator: processed_events, total_events, bytes_ingested.
Kevin: backend note — dedupe is expensive; if we enable dedupe during backfill we're increasing CPU and KV pressure. maybe run dedupe only for EU tenants for now.
Sam: ops-bot just reported: JobCount=142 queued, AvgWait=38m. pinging @ops for current capacity.
ops-bot: ReplayerAlert: 142 queued jobs, capacity_util=94%, fallback pools available=1. job-rate-limit=120/s.
Anna: proposal: 1) enable fallback to pool B for low-priority tenants, 2) soft-throttle per-tenant at 8 qps, 3) Surface progress widget in Console (metrics above), 4) add a circuit-breaker in router to stop new backfills if KV latency > 200ms.
Maya: sounds good. who can own the router circuit-breaker PR?
Devin: I can do the router piece, quick patch to add KV latency check + config flag `replay.router.kv_circuit_ms=200`.
Kevin: I'll scope the dedupe change — config flag `replay.dedupe.mode=per_region|off` and default to off for backfills.
Leo: I'll sketch the Console panel. need the metric names: replay.processed_events, replay.total_events, replay.bytes_ingested, replay.shard_id.
Maya: sample CLI for ops to manually trigger fallback if needed:
```
redwoodctl replay trigger --shard=23 --from=2026-03-01 --to=2026-03-05 --priority=low --route=pool-b
```
Devin: nice. make sure `redwoodctl` is updated to respect tenant quotas, else ops could accidentally flood pool B.
Sam: quick question — do we have telemetry to correlate backfill jobs to original ingest delays (late_event_reason)? would help prioritize replays.
Kevin: we have late_event_reason in raw events but not surfaced to replay coordinator. adding it would add metadata to job records; low effort.
Maya: timeline: router PR (Devin) by EOD tomorrow, dedupe flag (Kevin) in two days, Console panel (Leo) mock Wednesday, ops CLI patch quick today.
Anna: deployment plan: canary the circuit-breaker in staging, then roll to prod with 10% of replays on pool B for 2 hours, watch kv latency + per-tenant error rate.
Devin: will add a rollout policy: `replay.router.fallback_canary=0.1` and a kill switch.
ops-bot: CanaryStart: fallback_canary=0.1, affected_jobs=28, started_by=Devin, run_id=rb-2026-06-11-01.
Maya: please post the canary logs to #eng-sre. Also adding a simple dashboard tile under Console > Replays: Active, Queued, AvgWait, KV_latency.
Leo: mock link: https://console.internal/redwood/replays/mock — will iterate.
Sam: leaving note for oncall: if queue spikes >200 or KV latency >300ms revert fallback and open incident.
Maya: thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review canary metrics.
Devin: filing PRs now.
Kevin: will add schema for late_event_reason to job metadata.
Anna: documenting the soft-throttle behavior in the runbook after deploy.
Maya: closing loop: once progress panel is up, ops can triage high-value tenants first and we can avoid full replays for low-value noisy tenants. :thumbsup:
